recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not restore the original FHIR-40581 roadmap text; any broader refresh of Diagnostics roadmap FMM levels, ServiceRequest treatment, or incubator-resource wording should wait for FHIR-54965 or a successor final WG decision.
issue_request: FHIR-40581 was an Applied/Persuasive Orders and Observations technical correction asking to update the Diagnostics module Developmental Roadmap to reflect current activity for the module's resources. Its resolution supplied resource-by-resource roadmap text for Observation, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Specimen, ImagingStudy, ImagingSelection, MolecularSequence, GenomicStudy, and BodyStructure.
initial_application: The requested roadmap update was pre-applied in commit 1a3fadb445c304e186648da825bcf00a63844d59 and merged through PR #2868 at 35e3c2a00b2e22c49b49920803bbb7642ab2958a. Current HEAD still has that application in its ancestry.
additional_context: Later Applied Diagnostics module work superseded parts of the original wording. FHIR-50920 applied the Diagnostic Module - R6 Updates Confluence page and commit cefb308f4b8691afd6ae29eef993eb48bf8aba68 removed the older ServiceRequest roadmap bullet while preserving ServiceRequest in the page's Index/Table 1 context and moving ordering workflow discussion to the Workflow module. Later MolecularSequence/MolecularDefinition changes, Additional Resource cleanup, FHIR-50524's Specimen FMM3 correction, and R6 trial-use note cleanup also adjusted the same roadmap. FHIR-54965 is a later Triaged, unresolved follow-up for end-of-R6 roadmap and missing-use-case review, so it is not final source-edit authority here.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active source/diagnostics-module.html roadmap already reflects the FHIR-40581 application as modified by later final R6 module decisions already present on the combined branch. Restoring the older ServiceRequest or MolecularSequence wording from FHIR-40581 would reintroduce stale text and conflict with later applied context.
